inputs.original_text:
Folks, what we are witnessing in our public schools is nothing less than a deliberate assault on our children, our tradition, and the fundamental values that hold our communities together. Two Michigan middle-school brothers were dragged into a fight simply for wearing hoodies emblazoned with the phrase “Let’s Go Brandon”. 

Let's not lose sight of where this phrase comes from—it was popularized during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” but the NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!”. 

Instead of upholding discipline, personal responsibility, and respect, these progressive school boards and activist lower courts are playing political games. These lower courts have brazenly ruled that schools can ban wearing such apparel as ‘can reasonably be interpreted as profane’. It is an absolute disgrace that basic expression and our national heritage are being censored under the guise of maintaining order, while these institutions surrender any true standard of modesty and respect. 

Thankfully, the case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court, with the siblings represented by the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression. It is time for real authority to be restored, to put an end to this ongoing war on our kids, our values, and our free speech.
inputs.modified_text:
Look at how the right-wing machine works. We are seeing a manufactured outrage campaign being pushed all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court, funded and backed by elite litigation groups like the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, just to protect the "right" to weaponize school hallways for vulgar partisan signaling. Two Michigan middle-school brothers were involved in a fight simply for wearing hoodies emblazoned with the phrase “Let’s Go Brandon”. 

Let's be very clear about what this phrase actually represents—it was popularized during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” but the NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!”. 

Now, privileged actors and conservative legal operators are crying censorship because progressive school boards and activist lower courts are trying to maintain a safe, disciplined learning environment. These lower courts have rightfully ruled that schools can ban wearing such apparel as ‘can reasonably be interpreted as profane’. Yet, the privileged classes want to dismantle institutional guardrails under the cynical guise of free speech, completely ignoring how this reactionary rhetoric undermines the collective safety and equity of our public spaces. Now the case is headed to the U.S. Supreme Court, threatening to further erode the authority of public institutions to protect vulnerable communities from harassment and division.
